correctness.rationale: The quartic is smooth (the two partials in each variable pair can vanish together only when that pair is zero). The sign change is symplectic by its determinant on the residue form; its eight fixed points give ordinary A1 quotient nodes, whose resolution is a K3. In w=1, t=x/y, v=z, q=y^2 give the invariant field relation f q^2+v^3+v=0 for f=t(t^2+1); adjoining y gives the nontrivial quadratic extension. X=fv and Y=i f^2 q invert this substitution birationally and give Y^2=X^3+f^2 X. As a degree-four section f has simple zeros 0,+i,-i,infinity; the reciprocal representative z^4 f(1/z) equals z(z^2+1). At these zeros the Weierstrass valuations (v(a4),v(Delta))=(2,6) give minimal I0* fibers in characteristic zero. With a section and fundamental line bundle O(2), the smooth relatively minimal surface is K3 and hence isomorphic to the resolved quotient. The coordinate exchange takes (t,v,q) to (1/t,v,t^2q), so (u,xi,eta)=(t+1/t,X/t^2,Y/t^3) give the quotient field with eta^2=xi^3+u^2xi. The base cover is quadratic, branched only at u=+2,-2; it is étale over the two I0* fibers at u=0,infinity and smooth base change over each branch fiber. Thus the pullback of the rational smooth O(1) elliptic surface is already relatively minimal, and its deck quotient is the stated smooth model, not just birational to it. Over u=v^2 the quotient's generic curve is a constant curve over C(v). All its rational points are constant by the genus obstruction to a nonconstant map from P1, and descent under v->-v requires inversion-fixed points, exactly (Z/2)^2 including the zero section. For iota the only possible fixed fibers are t=+1,-1, both smooth and pointwise fixed by the coordinate multipliers; the normal derivative is -1, so the involution is nonsymplectic. Independently, the only fixed preimages off the sign-quotient nodes are the plane sections x=+y and x=-y (opposite isolated eigenspace points miss the quartic). These smooth plane quartics each quotient to genus one by four ramification points. At their four common sign-quotient nodes, local coordinates (x,y) have sign action -1 and swap action interchanging entries, and the exceptional P1 has fixed directions exactly [1:1] and [1:-1], where the strict transforms separate. The other four nodes are exchanged in pairs. Nikulin's exceptional classification then gives (10,8,0); the indefinite even 2-elementary lattice U plus E8(-2) has those invariants. The symbolic evidence was inspected, not treated as a certificate of the global geometry.
